main_body: A flat grass ground patch (terrain tile block) with sparse texture dots and a faint repeating 16px grid of lighter pixels
top_band: none: terrain ground surface, the column scan shows only uniform mid green with a 1-row lighter line repeated every 16 rows (tile seam)
evidence: Terrain kind: a flat ground patch of grass, not a standing object. There is no top/front structure to judge, and none is required for ground tiles. The column scan shows only repeated tile-seam lines on a uniform green, with no standing volume, so the 3/4 contract does not apply and nothing contradicts it as terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 5 distinct colours and a median of 5 colours per tile, against 80 distinct colours and 26 per tile for the grass reference. Flat-fill coverage is 20% where the grass reference has 0%. The grass is one mid green with a few sparse light and dark dots, and the repeated 16px seam lines make a visible grid pattern. The grass reference has clumps in several greens, tufts and a darker patch. Placed next to it, the candidate looks flatter and thinner, with a repeated stamp-like pattern.
